claim.statement: On 21 April 2026, SNN reported that six Shahid Beheshti University dormitory units, mostly girls' dorms that had housed about 2,000 students, had lost habitability and required complete rebuilding after U.S.-Israeli attacks; sports halls and some educational and research buildings were also severely damaged, including one research institute and internal labs assessed as 100% damaged.
claim.subject: Shahid Beheshti University dormitories
claim.object: six dormitory units and related educational/research infrastructure

evidence.summary: SNN quoted the deputy science minister / Student Affairs Organization head after a site visit and gave counts for damaged dorm units and affected students.

information_depth.rationale: The source reports named officials, damaged facilities, affected student count, and habitability status.

claim.statement: On 28 April 2026, ILNA reported Science Minister Hossein Simai telling parliament's education commission that 231 scientific centers had been targeted, that cutting international internet was one of the important challenges damaging university social resilience, and that the ministry was offering relief such as support packages for science-park firms with under 20% layoffs, special support for students whose homes were destroyed, and more flexible thesis defenses.
claim.subject: Iran's Ministry of Science
claim.object: higher-education infrastructure damage and international-internet resilience harm

evidence.summary: ILNA reported the minister's figures and mitigation measures from a joint parliamentary education-commission meeting.

information_depth.rationale: The claim records an official admission with specific damage count and policy responses, while treating the count as an official claim rather than independently verified damage.

claim.statement: On 23 April 2026, Iran Online quoted Sharif University's ICT director saying faculty international-internet access had mostly been restored through ministry servers and faculty mobile lines, but students still faced serious problems accessing international internet, external scientific resources, and international communication; students could use domestic university services, but Sharif had no independent authority to provide special student internet packages.
claim.subject: Sharif University students
claim.object: international internet and external scientific-resource access

evidence.summary: Iran Online interviewed Sharif's ICT director about faculty versus student international-internet access.

information_depth.rationale: The source directly quotes the university ICT director and distinguishes faculty, student, domestic, and international access.

subjects: Iran University of Science and Technology

claim.statement: On 30 April 2026, IranWire reported that the Iran University of Science and Technology student-rights working group said several students connected to Dey and Bahman 1404 protests were texted to send disciplinary defenses by email by 12 Ordibehesht despite remote university operation and more than two months of internet disruption; the group said the process contradicted 1403 disciplinary rules requiring in-person charge notification and defense.
claim.subject: Iran University of Science and Technology disciplinary process

evidence.summary: IranWire summarized the student-rights working group's reported SMS/e-mail disciplinary process and legal objections.

information_depth.rationale: The report is detailed but relies on a student-rights group rather than an official record.

assessment.uncertainty: Needs a primary student-group post or university response for full confidence.

claim.statement: On 30 April 2026, IranWire, citing United Students, reported that Ali Alirezai, a 1402-entry mathematics undergraduate at Sharif University, was arrested on 9 Ordibehesht; some recently detained Sharif students had been released temporarily on bail, while Mostafa Mohammadhasan reportedly remained detained and Fariborz Kohnzad remained unaccounted for after an earlier security-force arrest.
claim.subject: Sharif University students
claim.object: arrests, detention, bail release, and disappearance reports

evidence.summary: IranWire cited United Students for the Alirezai arrest, Mohammadhasan detention, Kohnzad disappearance, and bail releases.

information_depth.rationale: Names, dates, and statuses are specific, but the report relies on student-source reporting without official confirmation.

assessment.uncertainty: Needs official, family, lawyer, or primary student-channel confirmation.

claim.statement: On 21 April 2026, Melliun reprinted an IranWire / United Students report that 50 Birjand University students had received disciplinary sentences despite remote classes: about 30 were deprived of welfare services until graduation and about 20 were suspended for two terms counted against allowed study years; the report said many nonlocal students were absent from Birjand and could not attend hearings, and some did not receive SMS hearing notices.
claim.subject: Birjand University students

evidence.summary: Melliun reprinted an IranWire / United Students report with numbers and sentence types.

information_depth.rationale: The report gives numbers and sanction types, but it is secondhand opposition/student-source reporting.

assessment.uncertainty: Needs primary notices, student testimony, or university response.

question.text: Are university disciplinary cases and student arrests becoming a coordinated post-war crackdown, or are they still isolated campus-level reprisals?
question.resolution_criteria: Primary student-channel posts; university disciplinary notices; lawyer/family confirmations; Ministry of Science responses; counts across Tehran and provincial universities after 12 Ordibehesht 1405.
question.why_it_matters: A coordinated student crackdown would show the regime treating universities as a political threat even while it needs them for reconstruction and knowledge-economy recovery.

operations.rationale: The detailed Shahid Beheshti damage report explains why Shahid Beheshti dorm presence remained unavailable in the broader dorm-access roundup.
The ministry's higher-education damage and mitigation statement gives national context for campus closures and limited reopening.
The minister's admission that international-internet cuts damage university resilience is an official version of the Internet Pro/tiered-access legitimacy problem.
The Iran Online interview adds official operational detail to Sharif's partial reopening and faculty-versus-student internet gap.
Sharif's faculty-first and student-blocked access is a concrete university instance of tiered internet access.
Science and Technology disciplinary pressure is another campus response to student protest activity under remote/internet-constrained conditions.
New Sharif arrest reports deepen the same repression context as the Sharif class boycott over Parnian Khodabakhshi detention.
Birjand would indicate the disciplinary pattern extends beyond Tehran if corroborated.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v12 — campus rationing becomes campus discipline
synthesis.summary: The twelfth pass tightens the university picture. Official and near-official Persian sources now show that campus restriction is not only a convenience measure: SNN says six Shahid Beheshti dorm units, mostly girls' dorms for about 2,000 students, lost habitability and need full rebuild; ILNA reports the science minister telling parliament that 231 scientific centers were targeted and that cutting international internet damages university social resilience; Iran Online quotes Sharif's ICT director saying faculty access has mostly been restored while students still lack international internet and outside scientific resources. Student-rights reporting adds the coercive layer: IranWire reports Science and Technology students being pushed into email disciplinary defenses despite the internet cut; IranWire also reports new Sharif arrests/detentions; Melliun/IranWire report Birjand disciplinary sanctions against about 50 students. Net: universities are becoming a high-resolution crack. The regime needs laboratories, dorms, thesis defenses, and science-park firms for post-war recovery, but it is reopening them selectively while keeping students off global internet and under disciplinary threat.
synthesis.limitations: The infrastructure and internet-access layer is high confidence because it comes from official or near-official Persian outlets with named officials. The disciplinary/arrest layer is medium confidence: it is specific and current, but relies heavily on IranWire, Melliun, and student-source reporting rather than primary notices, lawyers, families, or university confirmations. Several aggregator hits were excluded after source-date checks showed stale Esfand 1404 material.

information_depth.rationale: The synthesis separates official campus-damage/access evidence from lower-confidence student-rights reports and carries explicit source-date exclusions.

operations.reason: v12 adds current higher-education infrastructure damage, faculty/student internet asymmetry, and student disciplinary/arrest reports to v11's campus access rationing.
